deepDive.title: It was never about the model. It’s about the harness.
deepDive.dek: What the FCA and FSB's latest warnings mean for remediation capacity, control design and correlated cyber disruption.

committeeQuestion.question: For one live platform or venue, which two or three conditions make it acceptable — and can we show they hold today?
committeeQuestion.why: The SEC's exemption and Anthropic's embedded-evaluation model make the point in different ways: the activity is only acceptable while particular rights, access and scrutiny conditions remain in force.
committeeQuestion.evidence: The agreed conditions, the relevant contract or rule, current access and rights records, the evidence trail, the last challenge, any breach and the decision taken.

committeeQuestions.question: If the provider, code path or market arrangement changed tomorrow, who could see the underlying evidence and challenge whether the conditions still held?
committeeQuestions.why: Embedded evaluation is useful only when the evaluator has practical visibility, while tokenised-market conditions depend on auditable code and continuing alignment between the instrument and its trading environment.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The access route, independent reviewer, relevant system or contract version, challenge record, response, and the decision on whether the activity can continue.

committeeQuestions.question: Could we find the affected asset, position or model quickly enough to meet the condition — before an exposure becomes an exception?
committeeQuestions.why: OSFI's implementation timetable and CISA's exploited-vulnerability additions both turn a broad control claim into a time-bound evidence question.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The authoritative inventory, applicable data and model record, remediation or calculation output, time-stamped result, unresolved gap and the decision record.

judgement.title: The conditions are the control.
judgement.editorialAngle: Operating conditions—not high-level approval—define the live control boundary.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 13 asked whether a changed live result still met its approved baseline. This edition asks whether the specific conditions for a provider, venue or control remain in force while it operates.
judgement.observation: Anthropic is putting independent evaluators inside its model-development process. The SEC has set conditions for tokenised-stock venues, OSFI has published its 2027 market-risk chapter, and CISA has added newly exploited vulnerabilities.
judgement.executiveJudgement: These are not broad policy tests. They bind a real activity to particular conditions: who can see the evidence, whether the underlying asset and rights match, how code is auditable, which data supports a risk measure, and how quickly a known exposure can be found.
judgement.implication: Choose one live external platform or market workflow. Write down the two or three conditions that make it acceptable, name the evidence that shows they still hold, and take any breach — not a generic assurance update — to the next risk committee.

topSignals.title: Embedded AI evaluation turns provider assurance into an access-and-independence question
topSignals.label: Independent challenge
topSignals.why: Assurance is only credible when an evaluator has practical access to the safeguards, evidence and operating context needed to challenge a provider.

topSignals.title: SEC’s tokenised-stock exemption makes venue controls a condition of market access
topSignals.label: Conditional market access
topSignals.why: Rights equivalence, auditable smart contracts, trading-halt alignment and disclosure become continuing conditions of a permitted activity.
topSignals.source: US Securities and Exchange Commission · Regulator · 2026-09-17

topSignals.title: OSFI’s 2027 market-risk standard sets a timetable for model and data evidence
topSignals.label: Implementation evidence
topSignals.why: The chapter turns a future capital standard into a present question about model, data-lineage and calculation evidence.
topSignals.source: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions · Regulator · 2026-09-10

topSignals.label: Exposure to action
topSignals.why: An exploited-vulnerability alert matters when the estate can be identified, remediated and evidenced before delay becomes an exception.
topSignals.source: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency · Regulator · 2026-09-18

topSignals.title: BIS puts critical third-party dependence inside the cyber-resilience test
topSignals.label: Continuing priority
